solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great success concerning voucher

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant, successful stroke
on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Someone got a real bargain thanks to a money-off voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a printed slip exchanged for goods or a discount, which is what a voucher is.

clue.text: Young bird allowed to follow wingless fowl

indicators.note: says the second piece comes after the first
a bird with both wings gone loses its sides, so the word fowl keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A fledgling permitted to tag along behind a flightless chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingless' strips both ends of FOWL, leaving OW, not OWL as it first seems.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a baby owl, so a young bird of a particular kind.

clue.text: A rapacious creature, I managed hospital area under parking

indicators.note: in a down answer the following pieces sit below the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A greedy hospital administrator boasts of running the ward beneath the car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Piranhas are flesh-eating fish famed for ferocious feeding, so a predatory, greedy beast.

clue.text: Sister with new uniform, head of nurses

parts.note: Uniform is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for the letter U

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here taken from nurses

explanation.surface: A senior nurse in fresh uniform in charge of the nursing staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' looks like the hospital rank; it is the religious sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order of women, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Cluster round king for morning meal

indicators.note: the cluster word is placed around the king letter

parts.note: a bunch is a cluster, as of grapes
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Courtiers gather around the monarch for a late breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunch is a late-morning meal combining breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Swimming style has fat go quickly

parts.note: butter is a cooking fat
to fly is to rush or move fast

explanation.surface: A swimming stroke that lets a heavy person go fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfly is a competitive swimming stroke with both arms swung over together.

clue.text: Relative is foul when last two letters never arrive

indicators.text: when last two letters never arrive
indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the word for foul fail to turn up, so they are dropped

parts.note: unclean means foul or dirty

explanation.surface: A family member grumbles that the post is awful because letters never come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last two letters' means the end of UNCLEAN, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a family member, the brother of one's parent.

clue.text: Property of informal talk on telephone

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a chat is an informal conversation

explanation.surface: Something owned by casual phone conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of personal property, a movable possession.

clue.text: Instrument popular with wine around

indicators.note: the wine word goes around the popular word

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that is a hit with the wine crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind musical instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Stuff beginning to rot in river at Cambridge

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

indicators.note: only the start of the word rot is used, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something starts decaying in the river by Cambridge colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to pack or force in tightly, which is to stuff.

clue.text: Hazel's maybe about to hit for six?

indicators.note: about signals the word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: hazels are one kind of nut, so the plural nuts is an example definition

explanation.surface: Is Hazel about to smash the ball out of the ground at cricket?
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name; it is the hazelnut. 'Hit for six' is a cricket phrase meaning to stagger or devastate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hit for six is to be shocked or overwhelmed, which is to stun.

clue.text: Work, eastern treat that's funny — The Mikado?

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: funny means odd or strange, signalling the word treat is jumbled

explanation.surface: A Japanese-themed treat that is comical: The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, so the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short, light comic opera, and The Mikado is a famous one.

clue.text: Old writer expired not achieving closure

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
ended means expired or finished

explanation.surface: An elderly author died without his story ever being resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left open-ended has no fixed limit or conclusion, so it lacks closure.

clue.text: Petrol has this running at once

indicators.note: running signals the letters of at once are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fuel keeps an engine running immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is sold by its octane rating, a measure of its resistance to knocking.

clue.text: Bright red vehicle belonging to me

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
mine means belonging to me

explanation.surface: Showing off a bright red car that is your own.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson colour or pigment.

clue.text: Returning insect is eaten by another helplessly

indicators.note: the turned insect goes inside the other insect

parts.note: another insect, here a fly

indicators.note: returning means the word for insect is read backwards

parts.note: a bee is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug comes back only to be devoured by another, unable to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns BEE into EEB, which 'is eaten by' FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feebly means weakly, in a way lacking strength, so helplessly.

clue.text: Give a reason for changing axle pin

indicators.note: changing signals the letters of axle pin are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic is asked to justify swapping an axle pin.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to account for it or justify it.

clue.text: Whitechapel killer in empty factory finding trifles

indicators.note: the killer's name goes inside the emptied factory
an empty word keeps only its outside letters, here from factory

parts.note: Jack the Ripper murdered women in Whitechapel, London, in 1888

explanation.surface: A notorious murderer found in a deserted factory amid knick-knacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Frippery means showy, trivial ornaments or things of little value, that is, trifles.

clue.text: Walk around Lake District?

indicators.note: the walking word goes around the lake letter

parts.note: to pace is to walk step by step
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A stroll around England's Lake District?
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a scenic region of north-west England; 'District' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A place is a locality or area, much as a district is.

clue.text: Ceremonial mass held by father

indicators.note: the mass letter is held inside the father word

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
M is the scientific abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A formal Mass is celebrated by the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ceremonial' is the noun here, meaning ritual display, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour and display, the stately show of an occasion.

clue.text: Damage on outside of round large tooth

indicators.note: the damage word sits on the outside of the other two letters

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
O is round in shape
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Harm to the outer part of a big round tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back grinding tooth.

clue.text: Mineral providing some chemicals

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the letters of chemicals is used

explanation.surface: A mineral that supplies certain chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Mica is a silicate mineral that splits into thin shiny sheets.

clue.text: Depressingly little put into do-it-yourself

indicators.note: the small word is put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: DIY is the usual abbreviation for do-it-yourself home improvement
small means little

explanation.surface: Gloomily, hardly any effort goes into home repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismally means gloomily or miserably, in a depressing way.

clue.text: Bag search regularly reveals it

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of search, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A routine bag search reveals something hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a pouch or bag-like structure in an animal or plant.

clue.text: Make a case for three successive letters to finish

parts.note: D, E and F follow one another in the alphabet
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A lawyer pleads for three letters in a row to round things off.
explanation.definitionFit: To defend something is to argue in support of it, which is making a case for it.

clue.text: Grant, say, protecting an island songbird

indicators.note: the name surrounds the word an as if guarding it

parts.note: Cary Grant was a Hollywood film star, so Cary is an example name

explanation.surface: A film star shields a bird found on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant looks like a verb or money award; it is the actor Cary Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a finch native to the Canary Islands, prized as a singing cage bird.
